text:
Dylan Holloway is the opposite of his teammate's story. Where Jimmy Snuggerud is finishing everything, Holloway has 6 goals on 8.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and the Blues have scored 4.2 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. He's still at 18 points in 23 games, because he keeps creating: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 80th percentile among forwards.

He's also one of the fastest players in the league, 94th percentile in top speed with 59 bursts over 20 mph, and he plays heavier than that suggests (52 hits). The Edmonton offer-sheet signing of 2024 has turned into a top-six winger: Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.8 wins last season, 20th among 401 forwards, though they also note his results ran ahead of his chances.

He has a four-game point streak, including two goals in Pittsburgh on Thursday. The worry is small but real: his ice time fell to 14.1 and 12.7 minutes the last two nights. If the minutes come back, our numbers say goals tend to follow chances like his.
